root_cause.text: The NOC_HDCP clock (BIT(11) in HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0) was being dynamically disabled during power-off operations, causing the NoC ADB400 port power down handshake to hang because the clock required for proper power sequencing was not available.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the dynamic clock gating logic that cleared BIT(11) in the `imx8mp_hdmi_blk_ctrl_power_off()` function for the HDCP power domain case, and instead ensures BIT(11) is always set in the `imx8mp_hdmi_power_notifier()` initialization sequence. This change prevents the NOC_HDCP clock from being disabled, which was causing the hang during the NoC ADB400 port power down handshake.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove incorrect or redundant HDCP power domain initialization that was causing improper hardware state or conflicts.
intent_record.what: Removed a case statement for IMX8MP_HDMIBLK_PD_HDCP from the imx8mp_hdmi_blk_ctrl_power_on function that was setting bit 11 in the HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0 register.
intent_record.how: This change removes the power-on initialization sequence for the HDCP (High-bandwidth Digital Content Protection) power domain. When the HDCP domain power-on is requested, the register bit will no longer be set, potentially leaving the HDCP block in an uninitialized state or causing it to fail to power on properly.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove incomplete or erroneous HDCP power domain handling from the HDMI block controller power-off sequence.
intent_record.what: Removed a case block for IMX8MP_HDMIBLK_PD_HDCP from the imx8mp_hdmi_blk_ctrl_power_off function that was clearing bit 11 of the HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0 register.
intent_record.how: This change eliminates the power-off sequence for the HDCP (High-bandwidth Digital Content Protection) power domain. When the power_off function is called with the HDCP domain identifier, it will no longer execute the clock control bit clearing operation and will instead fall through to the next case (HRV), potentially causing incorrect power management behavior for the HDCP block.

intent_record.intent_summary: Enable bit 11 in HDMI clock control register to complete proper HDMI clock initialization during power state transitions.
intent_record.what: Added BIT(11) to the bitmask in a regmap_set_bits() call for HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0 register, changing from 'BIT(0) | BIT(1) | BIT(10)' to 'BIT(0) | BIT(1) | BIT(10) | BIT(11)'.
intent_record.how: This change enables an additional bit (bit 11) to be set in the HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0 register during the power notification handler. This likely activates an additional clock control signal or feature that was previously not being configured, potentially fixing incomplete HDMI clock initialization.

Removing erroneous HDCP power domain handling from the power-off sequence (Hunk 1) prevents the improper clock disabling that was triggering the hang condition.

candidates.rationale: This line directly disables the NOC_HDCP clock (BIT(11)) during power-off operations. According to the root cause, this clock is required for proper NoC ADB400 port power down handshake sequencing. Disabling it causes the handshake to hang because the necessary clock for power sequencing is unavailable.

This line attempts to enable BIT(11) only during HDCP power domain initialization, but the clock should remain enabled throughout power sequencing. The incorrect handling of this clock in the initialization sequence (only for HDCP domain) combined with its unconditional disabling during power-off (Hunk 1) creates the vulnerability where the clock is not available when needed for proper power-down handshake.

bic_trace_step.reason: Line 294 contains the vulnerable construct: `regmap_clear_bits(bc->regmap, HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0, BIT(11));` in the IMX8MP_HDMIBLK_PD_HDCP case. This directly clears BIT(11) in HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0, which is the NOC_HDCP clock. According to the vulnerability root cause, this clock should NOT be dynamically disabled during power-off operations because it is required for proper NoC ADB400 port power down handshake sequencing. The function is a power-down handler (based on context of clearing bits/disabling clocks), and this commit introduces the HDCP case without protecting the NOC_HDCP clock from being disabled. The fix would require either removing this clock disable or adding special handling to keep this clock enabled during power sequencing.

bic_trace_step.reason: This function is a power-on handler that enables clocks for various HDMI block domains. At line 239, for the IMX8MP_HDMIBLK_PD_HDCP case, it only sets BIT(11) in HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0 during power-on. However, according to the vulnerability root cause, BIT(11) (NOC_HDCP clock) is being dynamically disabled during power-off operations, which causes the NoC ADB400 port power down handshake to hang. The vulnerable construct is present because this commit adds HDCP support but does not include the necessary fix to prevent the NOC_HDCP clock from being disabled during power-off. The code shows the clock being enabled (regmap_set_bits) but there is no corresponding protection or handling to prevent its dynamic disabling during power-down sequences. The fix would require additional logic to keep this clock enabled during power-off operations or to handle the power sequencing differently.
